items.prompt: Why does IDURAR embed invoice line items in the Invoice document but keep payments in their own collection?
items.answer: Items only exist inside their invoice, while payments stand alone
distractors: Embedding lets MongoDB enforce a unique index on each itemName
Payments are embedded as well, but inside the client document
Mongoose cannot reference subdocuments, so items had to be embedded
items.explanation: Items are owned and bounded: no identity outside the invoice, always read with it, never queried across invoices. Payments are created, edited, deleted and listed independently, so Invoice.payment holds refs to them.

items.prompt: An invoice totals 100 with no discount and no credit. Two payments of 50 are posted at the same instant, and both requests read the invoice before either one updates it. What does the invoice end up with?
items.answer: credit 100, but paymentStatus left at partially
distractors: credit 50, since one $inc overwrites the other one
credit 100 and paymentStatus paid, as $inc is atomic
credit 50 and paymentStatus paid, from the last writer
items.explanation: The guide is right that $inc never loses an increment, so credit reaches 100. But each request computes paymentStatus from the credit it read (0 + 50 is not 100), so both $set partially. The status is derived from a stale read.

items.prompt: What must be true of the MongoDB deployment before IDURAR could wrap its payment writes in a Mongoose withTransaction?
items.answer: It has to run as a replica set, not as a single standalone node
distractors: It has to use WiredTiger with the write-ahead journal switched off
It has to be a sharded cluster spread across at least three shards
It has to enable the Mongoose autopopulate plugin on every model
items.explanation: MongoDB multi-document transactions need a replica set (or a sharded cluster); a standalone node, the default dev setup, rejects them. Journaling and autopopulate are unrelated, and sharding is not required.

items.prompt: The guide lists indexes IDURAR is missing. Which one does it say would also close the duplicate invoice number race?
items.answer: A unique compound index on { number: 1, year: 1 }
distractors: A unique index on the Invoice.client field by itself
A compound index on { removed: 1, enabled: -1 }
A TTL index on Invoice.date to expire old drafts
items.explanation: With a unique {number, year} index the database rejects a second invoice with the same number in a year, whatever the application does. The {removed, enabled} index only serves the default sort.

items.prompt: Suppose IDURAR gains a second admin account. Admin A requests GET /api/client/read/<id> for a client that admin B created. What happens?
items.answer: A gets the client, as read filters only on _id and removed
distractors: A gets a 403, as read compares createdBy with the req.admin id
A gets a 404, as every lookup is scoped to the caller
A gets a 401, as that token belongs to a different owner
items.explanation: The generic read does Model.findOne({ _id, removed: false }). Authentication passed, and nothing compares createdBy with the caller, so any admin can read any record: an IDOR the moment there is a second user.

items.prompt: app.js mounts several routers. Which one, serving generated business PDFs, has no isValidAuthToken in front of it?
distractors: erpApiRouter, mounted on the /api path after auth
coreApiRouter, mounted on the /api path after auth
the invoice routes of erpApiRouter, on /api/invoice
items.explanation: app.use("/download", coreDownloadRouter) has no auth middleware, unlike the two /api mounts that list adminAuth.isValidAuthToken first.

items.prompt: A list request arrives with filter=email and equal parsed into an object such as { $ne: null }. What does the generic paginatedList do?
items.answer: It answers 400 Invalid filter value before any query runs
distractors: It runs the query, so every record that has an email matches
It casts the object to a string and so matches no record
It drops the equal value and returns the unfiltered list
items.explanation: paginatedList checks typeof equal === "object" and returns 400 "Invalid filter value"; only a primitive equal becomes { [filter]: equal }. This blocks the classic operator-injection payload.

items.prompt: A client sends PATCH /api/client/update/:id whose body contains removed: true and a new name. What does the generic update controller do?
items.answer: Saves the new name, and forces removed back to false
distractors: Soft-deletes the client, since req.body is the whole update
Rejects the body with a 400, since removed is not allowed
Ignores the whole body, since removed is a protected field
items.explanation: update.js sets req.body.removed = false before passing req.body to findOneAndUpdate, so removed cannot be switched on this way; the other fields are applied. The security checklist lists removed among settable fields; the code overrides it. Fields such as createdBy or credit are still mass-assignable.

items.prompt: An invoice has been soft-deleted. Someone still has its /download/invoice/invoice-<id>.pdf link. What does the download handler do?
items.answer: Serves the PDF, since its lookup does not filter on removed
distractors: Returns 404, since the lookup requires removed to be false
Returns 401, since the download route requires a valid session
Returns 410 Gone, since the invoice was marked as removed
items.explanation: downloadPdf runs Model.findOne({ _id: id }) with no removed: false condition, so a soft-deleted invoice is still found and its PDF served, and the route has no auth.

items.prompt: Every login pushes a new JWT into AdminPassword.loggedSessions. What removes old tokens from that array?
items.answer: Only logout; expired tokens otherwise stay in the array
distractors: A nightly job that drops tokens past their exp claim
isValidAuthToken, which pulls a token when it expires
A TTL index on loggedSessions that MongoDB enforces
items.explanation: authUser $pushes on every login; logout $pulls the one token (or clears the array when called without one). No other code prunes it, so the array grows with every login that never logs out.

items.prompt: Invoice.notes must become a required field on a collection holding a million existing invoices. Which deploy order does the guide give?
items.answer: Add it as optional, backfill old documents, then require it
distractors: Make it required now; MongoDB rejects old documents until fixed
Make it required with a default, which rewrites stored documents
Rename the field first, so each next save fixes the old documents
items.explanation: MongoDB stores no schema, so old documents lack the field; a required rule would fail their next validated save. Add optional, backfill, then tighten in a later deploy. A Mongoose default fills the value in memory, but stored documents are not rewritten until each one is saved, and MongoDB itself enforces no schema.

items.prompt: IDURAR stores bcrypt(salt + password), where salt is a random shortid kept beside the hash. What does the guide say that extra salt adds?
items.answer: Little, because bcrypt already salts each hash internally
distractors: Its main defence, because bcrypt by itself stores no salt
Secrecy like a pepper, because the salt is kept elsewhere
Speed, because the shortid shortens the bcrypt work factor
items.explanation: bcrypt generates and embeds its own salt in every hash. The prepended shortid is stored in the same AdminPassword document, so it is not a secret pepper; the guide calls it a talking point, not a vulnerability.

items.front: Name IDURAR's validation layers and which requests each covers.
items.back: Client form rules (UX only, never trusted); Joi at the boundary (invoice, payment, auth only); the list query guard rejecting object equal values; Mongoose schema rules on save/update (all models); the /public path-traversal guard. Generic CRUD entities get only Mongoose validation.

items.front: Authentication versus authorization in IDURAR: what is enforced, and what is missing?
items.back: Authentication: every /api route except login/reset passes isValidAuthToken (JWT signature plus loggedSessions membership). Authorization: none; queries never filter by createdBy and there is one owner role. Fine single-tenant, an IDOR once a second user exists; fix it in shared middleware.

items.front: What invariant does Invoice.credit cache, and how can it break?
items.back: credit === sum of the non-removed payments' amounts (and paymentStatus is derived from it). It is maintained by separate writes with no transaction, so a crash between the payment insert and the invoice update, or between invoice and payment soft-deletes, silently breaks it.

items.front: The data-model guide gives four kinds of schema change. Which are safe, and what is the trap with renaming a model file?
items.back: Additive optional field: safe. New required field: add optional, backfill, then require. Rename a field: dual-write, backfill, drop. Change an enum: migrate docs holding removed values first. Renaming a model file also renames its generated API route.
